newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Clinton tells Romania to stay the course for NATO.
newsitem.headline: Clinton tells Romania to stay the course for NATO.

text.p: BUCHAREST, July 11 (Reuhter) - U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday urged Romanians to stick to their dream of joining NATO, saying their country was "one of the strongest candidates" for membership in two years' time.

"I know that Romania would have liked to be among the first of Europe's new democracies to join NATO," Clinton said in remarks released to reporters ahead of delivery to a vast crowd in central Bucharest. "I welcome Romania's deep desire to contribute even more fully to Europe's security and strength. I want that too, for Europe, America and you, and I say to you today: Stay the course and Romania will cross the milestone."

Speaking in University Square, where dozens of students were killed during the 1989 rebellion which toppled communism, Clinton praised the political and economic reforms launched by the new centrist government this year. He said that as long as Romania pursued change, "America will be by your side."
"The door to NATO is open. It will stay open. And we will help you walk through it," he said. "NATO is committed to review aspiring members in 1999 and Romania is one of the strongest candidates."

Clinton, the first U.S. president to visit Romania in 22 years, led resistance to a broad initial wave of eastward expansion for NATO. A NATO summit this week in Madrid issued invitations to start talks on membership to Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, passing over Romania and Slovenia.

Despite the setback in Madrid, tens of thousands of Romanians jammed University Square in blazing sunshine to hear the president, shouting "Clinton! Clinton!" and "NATO! NATO!" and waving small Romanian and U.S. flags.
